sections.title: Detailed Brief Overview
rows: Study of **Continents & Oceans** comprising the Earth's primary physiographic divisions.
**7 continents**: Asia, Africa, North America, South America, Antarctica, Europe, and Australia.
**5 oceans**: Pacific, Atlantic, Indian, Southern (Antarctic), and Arctic.
**Alfred Wegener** proposed the **Continental Drift Theory** in **1912**.
Forms the fundamental physical geography base for **UP Assistant Teacher (Environmental & Social Studies)**.
Lithospheric plates, oceanic trenches, mid-oceanic ridges, and continental shelves.
High-yield factual questions regarding highest peaks, deepest trenches, and major straits.

cards.title: Continental Drift Theory (CDT)
content: All landmasses were united into a supercontinent named **Pangaea**.
Pangaea was surrounded by a mega-ocean named **Panthalassa**.
Pangaea broke into **Laurasia** (North) and **Gondwanaland** (South) separated by the **Tethys Sea**.

cards.title: Plate Tectonics Theory
content: Modern accepted theory explaining Earth's crustal movement.
Lithosphere is broken into major and minor **tectonic plates**.

cards.title: Ocean Relief Features
content: **Continental Shelf**: Gently sloping shallow region bordering continents; rich in fishing grounds.
**Continental Slope**: Steep descent connecting shelf to the deep ocean floor.
**Deep Sea Plain (Abyssal Plain)**: Vast, flat, sediment-covered plains covering the deepest parts.
**Oceanic Trenches**: Deepest parts of oceans formed due to subduction zones (e.g., **Mariana Trench**).

cards.title: Major Ocean Currents
content: Movement of ocean water in a continuous stream driven by prevailing winds and Coriolis force.
**Warm Currents**: Flow from equatorial regions towards poles (e.g., **Gulf Stream**, **Kuroshio Current**).
**Cold Currents**: Flow from polar regions towards equator (e.g., **Labrador Current**, **Peru Current**).
Rich fishing grounds occur where warm and cold currents meet (e.g., **Grand Banks**).

cards.title: Major Straits and Isthmuses
content: **Strait**: A narrow body of water connecting two larger water bodies (e.g., **Malacca Strait**, **Bering Strait**).
**Isthmus**: A narrow strip of land connecting two larger landmasses (e.g., **Isthmus of Panama**, **Isthmus of Suez**).

sections.title: Important Facts and Data
rows: Largest continent by area and population.
Only continent crossed by Equator, Tropic of Cancer & Capricorn.
Home to the Great Lakes and Laurentian Shield.
Peninsula of peninsulas; no active volcanoes.
Smallest continent; known as island continent.

sections.title: Ocean Statistics
rows: Largest, deepest, and contains Ring of Fire.
Half-name after a country; asymmetrical basin.
Smallest and shallowest; surrounded by North Pole.

items.definition: Trick: **'A A N S E E A'** -> **A**sia, **A**frica, **N**orth America, **S**outh America, **A**ntarctica, **E**urope, **A**ustralia.

items.term: Confusing Australia as an Island vs Continent
items.definition: Australia is officially classified as a **continent** (smallest), though often informally called an island continent.
Many confuse it with Mariana; the correct deepest point in the Indian Ocean is the **Java / Sunda Trench**.

items.term: River vs Volume confusion in South America
items.definition: **Nile** is the longest river globally, but **Amazon** has the largest water volume and drainage basin.
Do not write Mont Blanc; **Mount Elbrus** (Caucasus Mountains) is geographically the highest peak in Europe.
Remember that the **Atlantic Ocean** is 'S'-shaped, unlike the Pacific which is circular/triangular.

upscNotes.content: Memorize the exact depths and locations of the top 3 deep ocean trenches (Mariana, Puerto Rico, Sunda) as UP competitive exams frequently ask matching-type questions.
Do not confuse Laurasia with Gondwanaland when revising continental drift theory; remember India originally belonged to Gondwanaland before colliding with Asia.
Focus on the Isthmus of Panama and Suez Canal as they connect major continents and oceans, serving as high-probability geography questions.
Europe and Asia are technically part of a single landmass called Eurasia, separated artificially by the Ural Mountains for historical and cultural convenience.
Always associate the 'Ring of Fire' with tectonic subduction zones around the Pacific Ocean basin.

keyTakeaways: Earth's surface consists of 71% water and 29% landmass distributed unequally between hemispheres.
Alfred Wegener's Continental Drift Theory (1912) laid the foundation for modern plate tectonics.
Asia is the largest continent while the Pacific Ocean is the largest ocean.
The Mariana Trench in the Pacific Ocean is the deepest place on Earth.
Straits and Isthmuses are crucial choke points connecting water bodies and landmasses respectively.
Cold and warm ocean currents play a vital role in determining global climate and rich fishing grounds.
